# `plotBars()` {#fn-plotbars}

W01 checked the endpoints and row labels of an azimuth interval spanning north. [W01 results](w01-plot-geometry.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-plotbars)

```{=html}
<p>A row represents one measurement. Its horizontal bar spans the supplied value minus and
plus its uncertainty, and an optional mark shows the centre. A scalar uncertainty is
reused for all rows. Sorting rearranges measurements, labels and widths together.
Celestial overlays use the declination axis. The widths reflect the supplied
uncertainties and acquire a probability interpretation only from the measurement model.
</p>
<p>For a two-year epoch range, celestial targets are displayed as bands
covering their stored minimum and maximum declinations across the full plot
height. Single-year targets are displayed as lines.
</p>
```

[The quantity represented on the angular axis](fn-plot-skyscaper-pdf.qmd).

<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>val</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of declination or azimuth values.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>unc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Single value or array of measurement uncertainty</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>names</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of names of measurements in <em>val</em></p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>unit</code></th><td><code>&quot;Declination&quot;</code></td><td><p>(Optional). Label celestial overlays on the declination plot. Defaults to TRUE.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>xrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of limits for x-axis.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>yrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of limits for y-axis.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>sort</code></th><td><code>FALSE</code></td><td><p>Logical to control whether to sort the measurements by their declination

NULL uses the current style.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>geometry</code></th><td><code>if (missing(shade)) &quot;interval&quot; else &quot;bar&quot;</code></td><td><p>Use <code>"interval"</code> for sightline intervals with a centre point, or
<code>"bar"</code> for filled or outlined rectangles. Explicitly supplying the older <code>shade</code>
setting selects rectangles unless <code>geometry</code> is supplied.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.legend</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Display target annotations when <code>show.obj.label</code> is also TRUE.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>style</code></th><td><code>&quot;publication-colour&quot;</code></td><td><p>Analytical display style, either <code>"publication-colour"</code> (default) or
<code>"publication-mono"</code>. Monochrome uses grayscale and preserves line styles.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Draws orientation measurements and their uncertainties on the active graphics device.
</p><h5>Coordinates and interpretation</h5><p><code>unit</code> labels the measurement axis; it does not transform azimuths into
declinations. Celestial overlay values are declinations. Use them with
declination measurements, or convert measurements first using the appropriate
site and horizon. Bars show the supplied symmetric angular bounds, not fitted
confidence intervals. Use <code>az.pdf</code>, <code>coordtrans</code> and
<code>spd</code> when the full measurement distributions are needed.
</p>
